name: navier-stokes
title: Navier-Stokes: von Karman vortex street (DFG 2D-2 benchmark)
question:
Does a real dolfinx incompressible Navier-Stokes solve -- Taylor-Hood-ish
P2/P1 velocity/pressure, classic IPCS operator splitting, on a
gmsh-generated channel-with-cylinder mesh -- reproduce the DFG 2D-2
benchmark's von Karman vortex street: periodic, self-sustaining vortex
shedding off an off-center cylinder, with drag/lift coefficients and a
Strouhal number in the neighborhood of the published reference values?
hypothesis:
At Re=100 with the cylinder offset 0.005 above the channel centerline (the
DFG 2D-2 geometry), the wake behind the cylinder is linearly unstable: an
impulsively-started, initially near-symmetric flow should grow a small
asymmetric perturbation (seeded by the geometric offset and numerical
round-off) into a fully periodic, alternating vortex street, visible
directly as an oscillating lift coefficient (mean ~0, non-zero amplitude)
and an oscillating drag coefficient (positive mean, smaller-amplitude
ripple at twice the shedding frequency) once the flow leaves the startup
transient. The oscillation frequency, non-dimensionalized as a Strouhal
number St = f*D/U, should land in the neighborhood of the DFG reference
~0.30 even if this solver's mesh/dt (chosen for feasible wall-time, not
full DFG-grade accuracy) don't reproduce the reference Cd_max/Cl_max to
the last decimal.
objective:
Run the `vortex_street` composite (real dolfinx IPCS on a gmsh-generated,
cylinder-refined channel mesh) long enough to pass through the impulsive-
start transient into established periodic shedding, and verify (a) the
lift coefficient genuinely oscillates (not just noisy/flat), (b) the mean
drag coefficient sits in the neighborhood of the DFG 2D-2 benchmark's
Cd_max~=3.22-3.24, and (c) the shedding frequency's Strouhal number sits
in the neighborhood of the benchmark's St~=0.30.
description:
Wraps a single `CylinderFlowProcess` (real dolfinx IPCS -- see
`viva_fenics/processes/flow.py`'s module comment for the 3-substep
operator-splitting derivation, shared with the simpler lid-driven-cavity
`NavierStokesProcess`) in the `vortex_street` composite generator. The
domain is the DFG 2D-2 benchmark geometry: a 2.2x0.41 channel with a
radius-0.05 cylinder centered at (0.2, 0.2) -- built with gmsh OCC
(rectangle minus disk) and imported into dolfinx with 4 tagged boundary
groups (inflow/outflow/walls/cylinder) via
`viva_fenics.fem_gmsh.build_channel_cylinder_mesh`, mesh-graded from
`h_cylinder` right at the cylinder boundary out to `h_far` in the channel
interior -- the mesh's accuracy driver for resolving the shed vortices.
BCs: a parabolic inflow profile (mean U=1, peak U_m=1.5, linearly ramped
from 0 over the first `inflow_ramp_time` seconds -- an impulsive
full-velocity BC at t=0 was found to destabilize the explicit-convection
IPCS scheme during development), no-slip on the walls and cylinder, and a
zero-pressure "do-nothing" outflow condition. Each tick, `update()`
advances the flow by IPCS substeps and computes Cd/Cl via a real surface-
force integral (`sigma(u,p).n` integrated over the tagged cylinder
facets) plus the vorticity field (`overwrite` sensor outputs, same
convention as `NavierStokesProcess`/`DiffusionProcess.integral`).

Stability note (from development): dt=0.001 -- and even dt=0.001 with a
skew-symmetric convection form -- went unstable (NaN) partway through the
startup transient (~t=0.5s) at this mesh; dt=0.0005 does not. The
production run (`sims/run.py`) uses dt=0.0005, which is smaller than the
1e-3-2e-3 that suffices for the simpler lid-driven cavity, and cost 33.7
minutes of wall-time (6058 substeps) for 3.0s of simulated time on this
machine.

Achieved result (the committed run): a genuine, clearly alternating von
Karman vortex street. Lift crosses zero and begins oscillating by
t~=0.65s, and by the analysis window (t=1.5-3.0s) std(Cl)=0.41 with
Cl swinging roughly +/-0.6 to +/-0.8 -- still growing in amplitude toward
(not yet fully at) the DFG reference Cl_max~=0.99-1.01 by t=3.0s. Drag
settles to Cd_mean=3.03 / Cd_max=3.15 over that window, ~3-6% below the
DFG reference Cd_max~=3.22-3.24. The shedding frequency's Strouhal number
is St~=0.31 +/- 0.07 (Hann-windowed FFT, 3-point parabolic peak
interpolation; the +/-0.07 is the FFT's bin-resolution floor set by the
~1.5s analysis window, ~5 shedding cycles -- a plain rectangular-window
FFT's nearest-bin estimate alone, 0.33, is within measurement resolution
of the DFG reference ~0.295-0.305, not a precise ~11% offset from it). All
three land close to the reference neighborhood on a mesh/dt/duration
chosen for feasible wall-time rather than DFG-grade mesh convergence --
see the study's report for the full accuracy/runtime tradeoff discussion.

expected_behavior.name: lift-oscillates
expected_behavior.en: The lift coefficient genuinely oscillates once past the startup transient: std(Cl) over the second half of the production run exceeds 0.15.
expected_behavior.rationale: A non-oscillating (flat or monotonically drifting) lift coefficient would mean the wake never left its initial near-symmetric state -- no vortex shedding occurred. 0.15 sits well above the ~1e-3 startup-transient noise floor and comfortably below the achieved std(Cl)=0.41 (production run, analysis window t=1.5-3.0s), so it cleanly separates "no shedding" from the real shedding this run produced.

expected_behavior.name: drag-in-benchmark-range
expected_behavior.en: The mean drag coefficient over the analysis window sits in [2.7, 3.6], bracketing the achieved 3.03/3.15 and close to the DFG 2D-2 benchmark's Cd_max~=3.22-3.24.
expected_behavior.rationale: The DFG 2D-2 unsteady benchmark's published reference range for the periodic-regime drag coefficient is Cd_max~=3.22-3.24. The production run (this solver's feasible-wall-time mesh/dt, not DFG-grade mesh convergence) achieved Cd_mean=3.03 / Cd_max=3.15 over the analysis window -- ~3-6% below the reference. The band brackets that achieved result with headroom on both sides while still failing a spuriously low (near-Stokes-flow, ~1-2) or blown-up (>4) result.

expected_behavior.name: strouhal-in-range
expected_behavior.en: The shedding frequency's Strouhal number (Hann-windowed, parabolic-interpolated FFT peak of the lift signal) sits in [0.25, 0.40], bracketing the achieved St~=0.31 +/- 0.07 -- within measurement resolution of the DFG benchmark's St~=0.30.
expected_behavior.rationale: St = f_shed*D/U is close to universal (~0.2-0.3) for bluff-body vortex shedding across a wide Reynolds range, and the DFG 2D-2 reference is St~=0.30 specifically at Re=100. The production run's refined estimate (over the analysis window t=1.5-3.0s, ~5 shedding cycles) is St~=0.31 +/- 0.07 -- the +/-0.07 is the FFT's own bin-resolution floor at this window duration, not an error bar on the physics, and it fully covers the DFG reference. The band brackets that achieved result while still rejecting a qualitatively wrong (e.g. spurious high-frequency numerical) peak.

behavior_tests.name: lift-oscillates
behavior_tests.description:
std(lift_coeff) over the last half of the production run (after the
startup transient) must exceed 0.15.

provenance.note: 0.15 sits well above the ~1e-3 lift-coefficient noise floor observed during the ramp-phase transient in development, and comfortably below the production run's achieved std(Cl)=0.41 (analysis window t=1.5-3.0s), so it cleanly separates "no shedding" from the real shedding this run produced.

behavior_tests.name: drag-in-benchmark-range
behavior_tests.description:
mean(drag_coeff) over the analysis window must land in [2.7, 3.6],
bracketing the achieved Cd_mean=3.03 and close to the DFG 2D-2
benchmark's Cd_max~=3.22-3.24.

provenance.note: Schafer/Turek DFG 2D-2 reference Cd_max~=3.22-3.24 (unsteady case, Re=100) is the target this band is drawn near, but the band itself was fit around the production run's achieved Cd_mean=3.03 / Cd_max=3.15 (~3-6% below reference) on this solver's feasible-wall-time mesh/dt, not DFG-grade mesh convergence -- i.e. calibrated to the observed result with headroom, not derived from theory alone.

behavior_tests.name: strouhal-in-range
behavior_tests.description:
The Strouhal number (Hann-windowed, parabolic-interpolated FFT peak of
the lift-coefficient signal) over the analysis window must land in
[0.25, 0.40], bracketing the achieved St~=0.31 +/- 0.07.

provenance.note: Schafer/Turek DFG 2D-2 reference St~=0.30 (unsteady case, Re=100) is the target this band is drawn near, but the band itself was fit around the production run's achieved St~=0.31 +/- 0.07 (the uncertainty is the FFT's own bin-resolution floor over the ~1.5s/ ~5-cycle analysis window, not an error bar on the underlying physics) -- i.e. calibrated to the observed result with headroom, not derived from theory alone.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation currently depend on
navier-stokes; it stands as the investigation's fluid-dynamics
showcase, built directly on the validated dolfinx bridge
(poisson-validation) rather than on the scalar diffusion/reaction
studies.
